(By Sri.M.P.S., Advocate) Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT V/s Respondents: 1. Syed Fakir Shah,
S/o.Syed Bahadoor, Aged about 35 years.
2. Syed Bahadoor Shah, S/o.Miyan Shah, Aged about 60 years.
3. Syed Rahima Bee, W/o.Syed Bahadoor Shah, Aged about 50 years.
All are R/at.No.46, Muniyappa Garden, Masjid Road, Viveknagar Extension, Neelasandra,
Bengaluru.
(Placed Exparte) JU DG M E NT The petitioners have filed the petition under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents.

sentences.text:
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
The petitioner No.1 is legally wedded wife of respondent No.1 and their marriage was solemnized on 22.08.2013 at Thomas Function Hall, Dairy Circle, Bengaluru in accordance Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT with Muslim Customs and rites, in the presence of family members and elders.
Out of their wedlock, they have begotten one male and one female child to them.
It is submitted that, after the marriage, the petitioner No.1 was taken to the matrimonial home wherein the respondent's were look after the 1st petitioner cordially for a period of 6 months.
Thereafter, all the respondents insisted and demanded to bring more dowry from her parents.

In this regard, torture and humiliated the 1 st petitioner, even though she had informed the respondents that, the loan amount borrowed by her parents for the purpose of the Smt. Shama Anjum vs Syed Fakir Shah on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118258588/
1 said marriage is not yet repaid.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the respondents again insisted the 1st petitioner to bring gold ornaments from her parents house or else to bring money, in this regard, the respondents used to pick unnecessary quarrels with the petitioner No.1 for silly and unjustifiable reason and abused the st petitioner with all sorts of filthy, vulgar and indecent language.

Further, she submits that, on 17.10.2017, all the respondents picked unnecessary quarrel with the 1 st petitioner and assaulted the 1st petitioner and thrown out the petitioners Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT from the matrimonial home.

Even after 10 months, neither the 1st respondent nor the 2nd and 3rd respondents visited and enquired about the petitioners, hence elders of both the families advised the petitioners had resided with the 1 st respondent separately.
During residing separately with the 1 st respondent, he has not paid any amount for household expenses.

Further, she submits that, the petitioner had tolerated all human and illegal activities of the respondent with the fond hope that, in one or other day, they will change their mind and lead a happy marital life, but all the hopes are went in vein, on the other hand, all the respondents continued their ill-treatment and manhandled and treated as a maid servant without providing proper food and clothes.

Further, she submits that, all the respondents colluding with each other demanded dowry to the petitioner, when she failed to comply their illegal demands,
all the respondents abused with all sorts of filthy, vulgar and indecent languages,
hence on 28.03.2019, the 1 st petitioner had lodged a complaint before the Puttnehalli Police Station and the same has been registered in Cr.No.75/2019 for the offences Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT punishable under Section 498A, 323, 504,
506 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 3, 4 and 5 of DP Act.
The 1 st respondent is working as a Manager at Suguna Food Pvt., Ltd., and drawing monthly salary more than Rs.90,000/-, apart from that, he has rental income more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
Hence, petitioner prayed to allow the petition.
3. After the registration of petition, notices were issued to the respondents and notices to respondents duly served.
The respondents failed to appear.
Hence, they were placed ex-parte and matter set down for trial.
4. To substantiate her case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.11 and closed her side.

5. Perused the written arguments and affidavit of assets and liabilities of the petitioner No.1.
6.

The points that arise for my consideration are;
Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that petitioner No.1 has been subjected to cruelty of domestic violence and neglected by the respondents ?

Smt. Shama Anjum vs Syed Fakir Shah on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118258588/
2

entities.text: Shama Anjum vs Syed Fakir Shah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. Whether the petitioners further prove that, the respondent No.1 is having sufficient means and has deserted the petitioners ?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for maintenance?
4. What order?

She contended that, her marriage was solemnized on 22.08.2013 at Thomas Function Hall, Dairy Circle, Bengaluru in accordance with Muslim Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT Customs and rites, in the presence of family members and elders.
Out of their wedlock, they have begotten one male and one female child to them.
During the stay of petitioners in the house of respondents, the respondent No.1 has given ill-treatment to the petitioners and drove out the petitioners without providing any maintenance.

9. The petitioner averred in the petition about the ill-treatment and domestic violence committed by the respondent and also deposed as Pw.1 by reiterating the petition averments and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.11.
Pw.1 deposed about the ill-treatment given by the respondents.

The petitioner No.1 has produced the Ex.P.1 is the Marriage Photos, Ex.P.2 is the Certified copy of FIR,
Ex.P.3 is the Certified copy of complaint, Ex.P.4 is the Certified copy of head of the charge sheet,

Ex.P.5 is the Marriage Invitation Card, Ex.P.6 is the Birth Certificate of petitioner No.2, Ex.P.7 is the Birth Certificate of petitioner No.3, Ex.P.8 is the Rental Agreement, Ex.P.9 is the School Fee paid Receipts, Ex.P.10 is the HDFC and ICICI Bank Statements and Ex.P.11 is the Pay Slip of Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT petitioner No.1 for the month of August, September and October - 2023.
On perusal of these documents, relationship between the petitioners and respondents are not in dispute.
10. Despite of service of notice, the respondents have not appeared before the Court.
Hence, the contention of the petitioners averred in the petition is supported by the oral evidence, which has remained unchallenged and unrebutted.
There is no any reason to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

The Ex.P.9 is the 4 in numbers of school fee receipts of the petitioner No.2 and 3 and on perusal of these documents, it reveals that, all the educational expenses of Rs.74,500/- of children Smt. Shama Anjum vs Syed Fakir Shah on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118258588/
3 were paid by the petitioner No.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the denial of economic support to the wife and the child constitutes domestic violence under Section 3 of the DV Act., and i.e., immaterial whether the parties are still residing in a shared household or not.

11. The evidence on record goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 lived together with her husband in a domestic Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT relationship and there are sufficient evidence making out the essential ingredients of verbal, emotional and economic abuse, which fall in the definition of domestic violence as given in Section 3 of the PWDV Act.
There is no any reason to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have proved that, petitioner No.1 has been subjected to cruelty and domestic violence by the respondents and the respondent No.1 has neglected the petitioners without providing any maintenance.
With these observations, this Court answers the points No.1 and 2 in the Affirmative.
12. Point No.3 :
As discussed above petitioners have proved that, petitioners have been subjected to cruelty and deserted by the respondents.
The petitioners contended that, respondent No.1 has not provided any maintenance and also not made arrangements for residence.

Admittedly, the petitioner No.1 is working as a Recruiter in Resource Solution India Pvt Ltd., and received a total salary of Rs.82,549/- per month and after deduction received a salary of Rs.71,879/- (for the month Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT of October - 2023) as per Ex.P.11.

The petitioners have stated that,
the respondent No.1 working as a Manager in Suguna Food Pvt., Ltd., and drawing monthly salary more than Rs.90,000/-, apart from that, he has rental income more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, to substantiate the said contention the petitioners have not placed any evidence before the Court.

13. This Court observe that in the present case, the petitioner No.1 wife is highly qualified and earns considerable income per month, maintenance cannot be granted to the wife and she is having sufficient income to maintain herself and she is capable of maintaining herself.
However, it is bounded duty of the respondent husband to maintain his children's irrespective of his income or his wife's income.
Therefore, children's of petitioner No.1 are entitled of Rs.10,000/- each per month as maintenance payable by the respondent No.1, till they attains majority.
Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT 14.

The petitioner No.1 further sought for directing the respondents to pay a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-
towards jewellary which were sold by them.

But the petitioners have not placed any documents before this Court to show that, the respondents have pledged the petitioner's gold jewellers to the Muthhoot Finance and the said gold jewellers belongs to the petitioner No.1.
Hence, the contention of the petitioners cannot be accepted.
15. After going though the entire materials it is clear that, the petitioners are residing separately from the respondents.
The respondent No.1 being the husband of the petitioner No.1 and father of the petitioner No.2 and 3 is having responsibility of maintaining them.

After considering the facts and circumstances and status of the parties, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled maintenance of Rs.10,000/- each per month, till they attains majority.

With these Smt. Shama Anjum vs Syed Fakir Shah on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118258588/
4 observations, this Court answers Point No.3 accordingly.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act., is partly allowed.

sentences.text: A. The respondents are hereby  restrained from committing any domestic violence against the petitioners.
B. The respondent No.1 is directed to pay maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month to the petitioner No.2 and 3, from the date of petition, till they attains majority.
C. The respondent No.1 is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- to the petitioner No.1 towards damages and costs of the proceedings.

D. The respondent No.1 is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner No.1 towards education expenses of petitioner No.2 and 3.
Crl.Mis.No.46/2021 JUDGMENT E.

If above order in Clause-"B and D", are materialized, the respondent No.1 shall also directed to pay the amount ordered above with additional increase of 10% every year, from the month of February 2024, so that, petitioners shall not be compelled to knock the doors of the court again and again for enhancement of amount of maintenance, till the date, up to which, the said order remains in force.
However, the other reliefs prayed for by the petitioners are rejected.
Office is directed to supply the copy of the order to the petitioners free of cost.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by him, corrected by me and then pronounced in the Open court on this 16th day of February 2024)
VISHWANATH SAVADI METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE, TRAFFIC COURT- V, BENGALURU.
